name: Parent Costs for Products of Maximum Factors
statement: Let $M_1,\ldots,M_\ell$ be nonempty proper maximum classes of ranks $d_1,\ldots,d_\ell$, let $D=\prod_iM_i$, and put $R=\sum_i d_i$. Then $h(D)=b(D)=R$, $m(D)=\min_i d_i$, and $R-\min_i d_i\le a(D)\le R$. Adjoining one or more visible constant coordinates makes the auxiliary count exactly $R$.
proof: Each factor has a rank-$d_i$ zero-auxiliary parent and $b(M_i)=d_i$. Repeated product subadditivity gives $b(D)\le R$, while VC additivity forces every parent rank, and hence $h(D)$ and $b(D)$, to be at least $R$. The product-core formula gives $m(D)=\min_i d_i$, and $0\le b(D)-a(D)\le m(D)$ gives the displayed interval. The definition of $b$ gives the constant-extension assertion.
comments: The factors need not be geometrically realizable.
